newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore blue chips take breather, KIE jumps.
newsitem.headline: Singapore blue chips take breather, KIE jumps.

text.p: Singapore blue chips took a breather in the early minutes of trading on Tuesday after strong rallies last week, dealers said.
They said activity had quietened down since Monday and profit-taking in stocks that had run up were expected to continue in the short term.

The key Straits Times Industrials Index was marginally higher by 1.03 points to 2,179.06 after 35 minutes into the open. The wider DBS 50 index dipped 1.57 points to 551.24. Market volume was slight at 25.3 million shares with 47 falls against 34 rises.

Keppel Integrated Engineering (KIE) got a boost from punters who chased the stock up on news that Far East Levingston Shipbuilding (FELS) raised KIE stake to 20 percent as part of Keppel Corp's group rationalisation of its industrial engineering business.

"I think the gains will just be temporary," said a dealer. KIE rose Singapore $0.14 (US$0.099) to S$1.58 on 13.5 million shares which included the 13.3 million shares bought by FELS at an average of S$1.45 each.
Pacific Andes gained US$0.035 to US$0.505 after its interim profit rose 22.6 percent to HK$28 million.
